title: Application Retirement, Offboarding & Decommissioning (Microsoft Intune)
author_notes: pricing: T3 — multi-phase removal with license/data reclamation. Multi-component within one platform (Intune app assignment intents, supersedence, Entra groups, app-control/CA artefact cleanup) with conditional logic and irreversible operations; priced at $2,295 in the T3 band, above single-feature T2/T3 Intune solutions to reflect the multi-stage campaign + data/license reclamation effort, below the WSUS/troubleshooting T3 anchors that carry heavier tooling.

gov_variant decision: false. Research (Microsoft Learn US Government endpoints / Graph national cloud deployments) confirms the retirement MECHANICS (Uninstall intent, supersedence, wave targeting, artefact cleanup) are identical in GCC High / DoD; only portal + service + Graph endpoints differ (portal.azure.us, login.microsoftonline.us, manage.microsoft.us, graph.microsoft.us / dod-graph.microsoft.us). Documented inline (Overview endpoint table + every script accepts -Environment USGov/USGovDoD). No separate Government deliverable required. Where a control's sovereign availability is uncertain, guide says 'verify for GCC High'.

overlap boundary: this product owns the retirement PROCESS and the planned removal CAMPAIGN (decision record, impact analysis, staged uninstall waves, data/license reclamation, artefact cleanup, evidence pack). The sibling 'win32-app-uninstall-removal-failure-remediation' owns DEEP per-device Win32 uninstall FAILURE debugging. A per-device installer-level uninstall error here is treated as a straggler to be counted, contained, and ESCALATED to that sibling discipline — not re-diagnosed. Troubleshooting section is kept campaign-level (devices not checking in, partial fleet removal, Required-beats-Uninstall, reappearance, reporting gaps).
